deltas.subject: Fix Polymarket configuration validation
deltas.review_summary: Historical commit 2a3acb566f2aa3dd2ffe1f77cd55195608f6186a hardens Polymarket configuration at Rust credential, configuration, provider, and execution boundaries and projects validation errors through PyO3. It rejects blank trading overrides, validates and normalizes funders with signature-type identity constraints, rejects malformed instrument selections before HTTP, bounds retry durations including jitter, combines explicit and generated event slugs, aligns refresh defaults, and makes execution examples opt-in for live orders while retaining risk checks and scoped reconciliation. These mechanisms are relevant to the supplied adapter, testing, and live guidance; this review does not establish any present-day implementation or guidance gap.
deltas.rationale: Exact commit identity, subject and changed paths inventoried from git; complete per-commit source review has not been performed. No conclusion about NT skill impact.
evidence: crates/adapters/polymarket/src/common/credential.rs adds validate_env_override: explicit empty or whitespace-only trading secrets fail with a field-specific message directing callers to omit the field or pass None for environment fallback. Explicit nonblank secrets retain precedence. Unit tests distinguish blank, explicit, and omitted overrides. This is relevant to nt-adapters' Rust-owned authentication/configuration boundary and nt-testing's deterministic credential isolation policy.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/common/credential.rs deliberately filters blank Relayer API keys before calling the stricter resolver, preserving their environment fallback. python/tests/unit/adapters/polymarket/test_polymarket_factories.py tests None, empty, and whitespace Relayer keys, as well as omitted execution credentials and explicit private-key precedence using monkeypatched environment values. The trading-credential breaking change must not be generalized to the Relayer exception.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/common/credential.rs validates explicit funder blanks and parses nonblank resolved funders as addresses, trimming and formatting them canonically. crates/adapters/polymarket/src/execution/mod.rs parses maker and signer addresses, requires equality for EOA and distinctness for non-EOA signatures, and returns canonical maker addresses. Tests replace placeholder addresses with valid addresses and exercise malformed funders, EOA mismatch, and case-insensitive address equality. These are Rust-owned signing/account-identity invariants under nt-adapters.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/common/retry.rs extracts the existing 0.25 jitter fraction into a shared constant. crates/adapters/polymarket/src/config.rs uses it to validate both retry delays as finite, nonnegative, and representable as Duration after maximum jitter, and requires maximum >= initial. Tests include NaN, infinity, negative, reversed, oversized, zero, and normal values. This is configuration-time duration safety, not a change to shared RetryManager error classification or execution unknown-outcome policy.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/config.rs moves the 60-minute refresh default onto the builder field and makes Default delegate to the builder. Tests compare Default, builder, JSON, and TOML construction and verify explicit None disables refresh and an explicit interval is retained. This supports nt-adapters' typed-default consistency and nt-testing's configuration round-trip guidance.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/providers.rs adds validated_condition_id, requiring POLYMARKET venue, a 0x-prefixed B256 condition ID, and a nonempty ASCII-decimal U256 token ID. crates/adapters/polymarket/src/config.rs applies it to configured load_ids after uniqueness checks. Provider loading validates caller IDs before cache filtering or HTTP, and configured fetching propagates errors rather than silently dropping malformed IDs. This directly concerns nt-adapters' instrument identity and fail-closed reconciliation scope.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/config.rs centralizes event-slug resolution: explicit slugs precede builder-generated slugs, blanks are removed, and exact duplicates are retained only once. crates/adapters/polymarket/src/providers.rs uses that resolver for both provider initialization and configured refresh. Unit tests cover combination and overlap with a clock-boundary-resistant generated period; HTTP integration tests exercise both initialization and refresh and assert both slug queries and instrument sets. These are focused behavioral tests consistent with nt-testing.

crates/adapters/polymarket/src/python/mod.rs delegates provider and data validation to Rust config.validate(), retaining subsequent proxy validation. crates/adapters/polymarket/src/python/config.rs tests PyValueError translation for blank data/execution overrides and infinite retry delay, and updates the scoped-ID fixture. This matches the supplied bounded PyO3 configuration/error-translation lane without moving production validation into Python.

crates/adapters/polymarket/tests/integration/exec_client.rs replaces invalid scope placeholders with structurally valid instrument IDs across explicit-target, out-of-scope, duplicate-history, owned-binding, mass-status, fill, and position-report scenarios. crates/adapters/polymarket/tests/integration/python.rs likewise updates its factory-extraction scope fixture. These preserve the existing test purposes under stricter validation; they do not independently prove live reconciliation acceptance.

crates/adapters/polymarket/tests/integration/http.rs updates condition-ID fixtures and generated batch IDs to valid 32-byte hex values while preserving selection/filter composition, missing-versus-cached loading, 100-condition batching, and caller-filter scenarios. Its new malformed-ID test asserts an error, an unchanged empty store, and no market HTTP queries. This is relevant to nt-testing's observable-state assertions and mock-boundary testing requirements.

crates/adapters/polymarket/examples/node_exec_tester.rs changes DRY_RUN to true and documents explicit live-order opt-in. examples/live/polymarket/exec_tester.py and examples/live/polymarket/updown_smoke_tester.py also default to dry run and remove explicit risk bypass. The Up/Down example adds the resolved instrument to load_ids, shares provider configuration with execution, and sets both disconnect timeout and post-stop delay to 30 seconds. These map to nt-live's safety, reconciliation, and bounded shutdown concerns; the 30-second setting is venue/example-specific, not a replacement for the current node shutdown-result contract.

crates/data/src/engine/handlers.rs: WarmupBuffer<T> shares Rc<RefCell<Option<Vec<T>>>> across clones. hold copies incoming items into the vector while it is Some; release takes the vector and leaves None, so subsequent handler calls pass through. deltas.subject: Support binary option expiry revisions during replay (#5511)
deltas.review_summary: Historical commit 838402a3c0f602aa8309a3a4b2e8fc82d5a9241e supports binary-option expiration revisions during replay by applying instrument updates before exchange routing, canceling obsolete expiration timers from both the clock and accumulated events while preserving shared timers, and scheduling eligible revised expirations. The simulated exchange permits expiration changes only between binary-option instruments and processes past-due updates immediately. The matching engine retains venue status while expiration blocks trading pending resolution, restores that status for eligible expiration revisions, and treats zero expiration as unset. These mechanisms are relevant to the supplied backtest and testing guidance; this historical review does not establish a current documentation gap or runtime readiness.
deltas.rationale: Exact commit identity, subject and changed paths inventoried from git; complete per-commit source review has not been performed. No conclusion about NT skill impact.
evidence: crates/backtest/src/accumulator.rs adds cancel_timer(name), which removes heap entries with the matching timer-event name. This covers expiration callbacks already advanced off the clock and is relevant to nt-backtest's deterministic event ordering and time-advancement guidance.

crates/backtest/src/engine.rs handles a peeked DataRef::Instrument before ordinary exchange routing: it records the previous expiration, sets exchange time to ts_init, and applies update_instrument. Instrument rows are then filtered out of route_data_to_exchange, avoiding a second update there. The iterator is reborrowed after scheduling. This is relevant to nt-backtest's Rust-owned replay sequencing.

crates/backtest/src/engine.rs cancels the previous venue/expiration timer from both the kernel clock and accumulator only when expiration changed and no instrument on that exchange still uses the old expiration. It schedules a revised expiration only when it is at or after ts_init and expiration has not already been processed. This directly relates to shared-timer correctness and latency-preserving deterministic simulation.

crates/backtest/src/exchange.rs retains the expiration-equality restriction except for BinaryOption-to-BinaryOption updates. After updating the matching engine and instrument map, it invokes expiration processing when the revised expiration is strictly before exchange time. The rejection test switches to OptionContract, preserving evidence that other instrument types cannot revise expiration.

crates/execution/src/matching_engine/mod.rs changes pending_resolution from bool to Option<MarketStatus>, initializes and resets it to None, saves the prior venue status when entering pending resolution, and keeps the effective market closed while canceling open orders. Status actions update the saved status while resolution is pending. Successful settlement clears the saved state, and order validation continues to reject while it is present.

crates/execution/src/matching_engine/mod.rs restores the saved venue status only when an instrument requiring pending resolution changes expiration, expiration is not processed, no explicit instrument close exists, and the revised expiration is absent, zero, or future. Timestamp-triggered expiration explicitly excludes zero. These are matching-state invariants relevant to nt-backtest's matching ownership and nt-testing's lifecycle-state assertions.

crates/backtest/src/engine.rs adds parameterized latency tests for revisions before or at the old expiration, shared expiration timers, and already-settled instruments. Assertions check fill price and event time as well as expiration state and market status, providing mechanism-specific ordering evidence consistent with nt-testing's deterministic Rust test policy.

The binary-option replay regression matrix in crates/backtest/src/engine.rs covers unchanged, finer, coarser, and precision-changing ticks; earlier, later, due-now, past-due, pending-resolution, and zero expirations; and close/pause venue states. It checks matching state before instrument subscribers run, order cancellation or acceptance, book clearing, sibling expiration independence, open positions, repeated runs, timer cleanup, and restoration of original cache and matching state after reset.
